title: Slow-Roasted Lamb Shoulder
subtitle: Fall-apart lamb with garlic and rosemary
excerpt: Four hours in a low oven turns a bone-in lamb shoulder into tender, pull-apart meat. Stud it with garlic and rosemary and leave the oven to do the rest.
sourceNotes: Classic British slow-roast technique. Low temperature and long cook time break down the collagen in the shoulder into gelatin, keeping the meat moist.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze pulled meat in portions with a little of the cooking juices for up to 3 months.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 130 or gas 2. Low and slow.

content.text: The lamb needs very little attention once it is in the oven. Give it a full 4 hours and it will fall from the bone.
Heat the oven to 150 degrees C. Take the lamb out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.
Use a small sharp knife to make 16 deep cuts all over the lamb. Push a piece of garlic and a small sprig of rosemary into each cut.
Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, and cumin. Rub all over the lamb. Season generously.
Place in a roasting tin. Cover tightly with foil. Roast for 3 hours 30 minutes.
Remove the foil. Increase heat to 200 degrees C. Roast for a further 30 minutes to colour the skin.
Remove from the oven. Tent loosely with foil and rest for 20 minutes before pulling apart with two forks.

items.symptom: Meat is still tough after 4 hours.
items.cause: Oven ran cool or the shoulder was very large.
items.fix: Cover again and roast for another 30 to 45 minutes.

items.symptom: Outside is dark but meat inside is dry.
items.cause: Foil removed too early and heat was too high.
items.fix: Keep foil on for the full slow period; only uncover at the end.

items.symptom: Very little liquid in the tin for gravy.
items.cause: Lean shoulder or cooking without any added liquid.
items.fix: Add 150ml water to the tin before covering with foil.
